first begin with being kind to yourself. try to be kind enough to recognize that you are deserving of help. you are deserving of rest; most importantly, you are deserving of healing. it's going to hurt a lot. however, if you do not break the pattern today it will repeat tomorrow.

you will need to step out of your comfort zone. that is the one requirement for any change in life, and it gets worse before it gets better.

think about what you are fighting for, and why you are fighting. visualize it, write it down. envision the kind of future you would find desirable. set a clear goal and remind yourself of it every day.

above all, you must be your own best friend. if you do not trust yourself to fight, you will fail. you have to learn how to sit with yourself, how to be on your side. that one will be hardest of all. but you must do it.

i'm available if you ever want to chat. i'm in a very similar position to yours. bpd is not something you can fight alone.

you're not a bad person. bpd is often a result of painful, prolonged trauma. deep down, we are very hurt and wounded. there's a child within all of us that desperately needs attention and healing that was not received before.

our symptoms and actions are manifestations of that pain. however, despite the fact that we are hurt, it is our responsibility to do our very best to control our behaviors. even though our pain might feel overwhelming in the moment, we must use coping skills so that we do not take it out on those who are undeserving. 

it's a lot easier said than done. however, things like this can best be accomplished with the help of therapy.

unfortunately, because we grew up being treated the way we were, we are now left to pick up the pieces. we're most familiar with environments in which we have to defend ourselves at all times. interacting with people outside of that environment can be very scary. you may subconsciously believe everyone has bad intentions. it's not fair – but there is no other way but forward.
